ListItems.Title: Crocodile Museum
ListItems.Description:
The Crocodile Museum is located next to the Kom Ombo temple, north of Aswan. This museum has highlighted the crocodile-headed god Sobek since it was opened in 2012. Its main exhibition hall displays the mummified mummies of Nile crocodiles. The longest crocodile was 4.30 m, while the smallest was 2 m.

ListItems.Title: Zoological Museum, at the Giza Zoo.
ListItems.Description:
Today we take you on a virtual tour in one of the oldest museums in the Middle East, the Zoological Museum, at the Giza Zoo.Where you can see rare skeletons and mummified models of various animals, birds and wild reptiles. Enjoy the tour and happy Easter to you all.Special thanks to the Ministry of Agriculture.

ListItems.Title: Mummification Museum
ListItems.Description:
Mummification museum in Luxor (ancient Thebes), intended to provide an understanding of the process to preserve the body. The ancient Egyptians not only applied embalming to dead humans but also to many animals (Cats, dogs, crocodiles…. etc.). God Anubis(the Jackal) was the god of embalming and mummification.

ListItems.Title: The work of the Egyptian archaeological mission in Wadi Abu Saubeira
ListItems.Description: The work of the Egyptian archaeological mission in Wadi Abu Subeira in the Eastern desert northeast of Aswan, uncovered a series of royal rock inscriptions. Dating back to the end of the Neolithic period, the inscriptions depict Egyptian royal symbols, along with many animals such as giraffes, elephants and crocodiles The work of the Egyptian archaeological mission in Wadi Abu Subeira

ListItems.Title: Canopic Jars of Isetemkheb
ListItems.Description:
During the mummification process, certain organs of the deceased, namely the liver, lungs, intestines and stomach, would be mummified, wrapped separately and then placed in four “canopic” jars.

ListItems.Description: This luxurious chess set consists of 32 chess pieces inlaid with 425 stones from diamonds and decorated with colored enamel. The chess pieces take the form of humans and animals. The human pieces reflect the rank of their chess counterparts, with the king piece representing the person of a ruler, and the pawns riflemen. ListItems.Title: The Journey of the Holy Family to Egypt
ListItems.Description: This unique roundel represents the Journey of the Holy Family to Egypt woven on a red background. In the center, in a square frame, the Virgin Mary -with the halo encircled her head- seats on the donkey carrying Christ-child. Behind her there is a building. ListItems.Title: Narmer Palette
ListItems.Description: The Narmer Palette contains some of the earliest hieroglyphic inscriptions ever found. It is thought to depict the unification of Upper and Lower Egypt under King Narmer. On one side, the king, wearing the Red Crown of Lower Egypt, marches in a victory procession. ListItems.Title: Coptic Oil Lamps
ListItems.Description: The ancient Egyptians excelled at pottery making since the dynastic period, as pottery was essential for carrying out daily necessities. Pottery was used for food preparation and for storage. It was also used for lighting. These oil lamps became known as “masarij.” The industry was well-supplied by the Nile silt. in the Coptic period the oil lamps resembled those made in ancient and Roman Egypt...

ListItems.Description:

The museum’s display scenario broadly reflects the different aspects of human civilization and culture in general, while shedding light specifically on ancient Egyptian civilization. This is done through a selection of historical objects that were carefully chosen from museum storage rooms.
